Each Bernhardt-Bernstein neutron sensor, which contains six liquid scintillator tubes filled with 6%-by-volume ethylene chloride solution surrounded by a polyethylene neutron reflector, was designed to identify neutrons passing through orthogonal steel plates. The performance of this neutron detector was evaluated using data from three low-muon periods in 2019, 2020, and 2021, with additional simulation support. Observations indicated that the detector successfully identified neutron hits, including their associated spatial and temporal characteristics. It also demonstrated correlation with simulated neutron hit distributions. Furthermore, the data supported the validity of the anti-coincidence method employed to eliminate false neutron signals associated with beam-halo protons.

Ground-based observations of planetary movements are crucial in validating the findings of space-based missions like Kepler and TESS. Although these space-based missions can detect planetary transitions, they are often incapable of determining the planet's mass or its inclination to the line of sight. As a result, ground-based surveys that specialize in observing the shifts in stellar spectra are now more critical than ever before. To maximize the effectiveness of these surveys, researchers have shift their focus from simply finding many planets to discovering significant ones. Several factors influence the decision to target the most relevant exoplanets for follow-up studies, including avoiding duplicates across teams, the age of the star, and whether the planet resides within the habitable zone. Observations of the transited stars revealed encoded information from the system's formation, such as the presence of water and the presence of planetary companions. Moreover, the presence of planetary atmospheres can be analyzed through a process known as transmission spectroscopy, while the ingestion of planets is sometimes triggered by stellar system evolutions, such as the movement of planets towards the star.

The growth of Information Technology has significantly altered how information is shared, making it necessary to convert printed documents into digital formats.  There has been an increase in fraudulent activities lately.  To prevent such account-related fraud, a system was devised which employs ID card extraction via OCR and NLP for verification purposes.  Optical Character Recognition, a technology that enables the conversion of images to text, can also be used to convert an Indonesian ID card or KTP into text format.  This facilitates easier data entry for service operators.  To enhance accuracy, the extracted text was further corrected using Natural Language Processing.  When tested, the accuracy, precision, and overall score for name extraction from ID cards were all found to be 100 percent.

Quantum harmonic oscillators were computationally analyzed in their ground state with either steady-state driving forces varying in intensity or driving forces that changed over time. Calculations of position expectations were carried out for multiple scenarios of mass, angular frequency, and the lambda parameter in both cases. Constant driving led to coherent states, with theoretical predictions closely matched by both simulation approaches. A discrete-time lattice Metropolis algorithm was used to evaluate the imaginary time path integral for these simulations.

The Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack effect significantly impacts the rotational states of small asteroids by exerting a net torque resulting from solar radiation reflected and re-emitted by the surface. As a consequence of this phenomenon, the rotation period of these asteroids gradually changes, which can be best measured through light curves as the phase shift accumulates over time in a quadratic manner. To study this effect in detail, researchers collected archived data and conducted new photometric observations for asteroids 1992 SK, Geographos, and Toro, before utilizing a light curve inversion method to match their shapes and rotation characteristics. By modeling the YORP effect and incorporating other relevant parameters into their analysis, scientists were able to detect the YORP acceleration in three asteroids and found that the YORP acceleration in all ten detected cases was positive, accelerating their rotations. Furthermore, incorporating dark regions into shape models reduced mismatch values, which suggests that these shadows may have a greater effect on the asteroid surfaces than previously anticipated.

The youth are increasingly relying on Instagram as a source of information, with political figures leveraging the platform to disseminate opinions and agendas. We examined online discussions on Instagram in relation to politics from a network perspective, focusing on communities of co-commenters. Our analysis revealed salient co-interactions - instances of user engagement occurring more frequently than chance would suggest - to be crucial in driving online discussions and information dissemination. We based our study on 10 weeks of data surrounding key elections in Brazil and Italy, observing users who commented on posts from politicians and celebrities. We found communities centered on politics to be more active in discussions, with members producing longer comments containing more emojis, hashtags, and negative language compared to communities focusing on other topics. Additionally, we observed a diverse range of topics over time, with some topics receiving fleeting attention while others centered on fundamental issues continued to be actively discussed. Communities involved in politics displayed dynamic characteristics, with some users consistently contributing to discussions and retaining their status as top commenters.

We show that any subgroup of homeomorphisms of a compact surface that fix the boundary, whose action within the surface's interior is highly transitive, cannot be topologically compact when using the compact-open topology's inherited structure.

Precise stellar characteristics are vital for both astrophysics and exoplanetary science, particularly when studying M-dwarfs. Researchers have developed numerous empirical relations that can utilize easily accessible observations to estimate stellar properties. However, these relations are often presented in a simplistic form, neglecting the complex non-linear connections between variables and potentially skewing the estimated uncertainties. Our study presents a comprehensive Bayesian framework that incorporates numerous empirical relations, stochastic errors, and any inherent biases within each relation. This approach is statistically robust, seamlessly integrating the complex interactions between different variables. Our method yields a nuanced understanding of the stellar parameters for a M-dwarf sample selected specifically for the JWST's EXCITING experiment, showcasing its effectiveness in forecasting the kind of exoplanetary systems this mission will be capable of characterizing.

Confining modes at the edge, known as line waves, can propagate on the boundary between two specially designed electromagnetic interfaces that maintain mirror symmetry properties.
Studies have previously analyzed line waves in theory and in practice, revealing their occurrence at both microwave and terahertz frequencies.
It has also been demonstrated that these waves can occur when there's a sudden change from a negative to a positive symmetric resistance and uniform surface reactance present.
Characteristics of line waves include highly confineable mode propagation, polarization dependent on direction, and unique localized field enhancements.
A new study proposes a graphene patch structure, showing that the occurrence of both line waves and moiré patterns can be utilized to create compact devices with multiple functions.
The design involves tuning occurrence of line waves by adjusting the surrounding uniform resistive loads, and introducing a moiré pattern line wave by changing the periodicity of the nonuniform loads.
This new structure demonstrates the potential for integrating multiple occurrence conditions within a compact device, and further shows the possibility of introducing gradient loads to create a supercell with a controllable phase shift.

Although a key function in database management, query evaluation classification lacks comprehensive guidelines when dealing with self-joined queries. This study investigates the impact of self-joins on the complexity of enumerating database results, building upon existing research. By extending analyses to include arbitrary partial orders and insights from recent findings, this work compares different scenarios, including cases with and without self-joins. It provides enhanced conditions for efficiently enumerating high-complexity queries and introduces new, unaddressed questions. As a result, this research expands the framework for analyzing enumeration complexity of database queries.

Multiple formal models can equivalently define functions that map infinite strings to other infinite strings, including MSO-transducers, streaming transducers, and certain two-way transducers. However, even when restricted to single passes through the input, some functions in these models can still be undecidable by Turing machines with infinite input, despite being defined by finite-state machines. To address this issue, a new decision-making approach is proposed for determining whether a specific function is computable and if so, to create a corresponding Turing machine. 

For the type of functions in question, being computable is equivalent to having a specific property called continuity, effectively simplifying this decision process. To further facilitate this check, a type of automated tool is designed to verify if a given transducer system is free from infinite loops. Deciding the computability of these functions is equivalent to analyzing these tools for a specific type of associated relation defined by the transducer, and if this function is continuous, the transducer can be converted into a descriptive rule known as an MSO formula. 

The proposed decision process involves constructing a specialized automated tool based on the given transducer's input, and using this, a corresponding descriptive formula can be found using a systematic search method.

Researchers have analyzed collision data with an integrated luminosity of 3 inverse femtobarns, and through amplitude analysis of specific two-body decay events, have discovered that the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons exhibits a higher fraction of longitudinal polarization than the $B^0_s$ decay to the same mesons. Furthermore, this difference in longitudinal polarization was utilized to determine the branching fraction of the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons.

Machine learning models can effectively unravel complex systems and generate models that accurately reflect underlying patterns. A computational framework known as reservoir computing has been highly successful in analyzing various dynamic patterns and predictions across multiple disciplines. The development of a novel approach, the spherical reservoir, leverages the principles of spin physics and incorporates universal approximation capabilities to improve upon traditional reservoir computing. The advantages of this new method are evident through a comparative analysis of a dynamic approach and unrelated domains such as weather patterns and social media dynamics. The results demonstrate that the spherical reservoir requires significantly less training data, offers better generalization to new data, and provides more accurate predictions in real-time. The implementation of this approach using a spherical processor also proves that it matches classical computing performance while offering the potential for a massive performance boost when combined with quantum reservoir computing.

A new bias-corrected estimator has been created for the mean absolute deviation of a median regression model, addressing the problem of irregularity that typically hinders conventional bias reduction.  To overcome this limitation, a specific alternative strategy was implemented.  Establishing the bias correction involves verifying the local asymptotic normality property and a specific Bahadur-Kiefer representation.  Developed within the context of a traditional asymptotic framework, this proposal appears to retain effectiveness in high-dimensional settings, as evidenced by simulation results.

To address scalability issues with Eulerian methods for finding optimal controllers under constraints and worst-case disturbances in variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs formulations, we've developed a second-order successive sweep algorithm for calculating the reachable state space. This approach, which assumes a continuous and smooth Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, enables us to determine the states that can be reached within a given time frame under worst-case conditions and state feedback control.

Multi-Layer Perceptrons are particularly effective at generating accurate
low-dimensional representations of data, such as images, shapes and light
fields. Despite advancements using periodic activations or positional
encodings for spatial representation, there has been a lack of research
focusing on simple methods. We propose a straightforward approach that
achieves lossless representation of grayscale images, color images, video
sequences, and even 3D models. Moreover, our method surpasses the
current state-of-the-art in video compression when evaluated at various
levels of representation dimension, offering an efficient solution to
representing video data.

The underlying mechanisms of the ventral temporal cortex's animacy organization remain contentious, suggesting that animacy exists along a spectrum rather than a binary divide. While some researchers suggest the continuum reflects either a part-whole relationship or the frequency of entities appearing together, other researchers propose explanations based on movement capability or value-based assignment of entities to motion or static categories. To test these hypotheses, a deep artificial neural network was trained to recognize a broad spectrum of combinations of images from different frequencies of animals and objects, leading to the creation of 50 distinct combinations to train 25 participants on. Subsequent analysis using generalized linear models revealed that the frequency-based hypotheses best explained the ventral temporal cortex's animacy organization, with the part-whole relationship also playing a role but with limited influence. This study's results suggest that frequency-based hypotheses offer a more generalizable explanation of frequency-based patterns in image frequency, with frequency-based explanations of animacy organization best fitted by unique animal/object frequency, and this explanation also applied when controlling for image frequency, with the part-whole relationship also playing a role but with limited influence.

The study proves the nonexistence of Landau-Siegel zeros or confirms quantum unique ergodicity for GL_2 Hecke-Maass newforms at a calculable pace, supported by the broader conclusion that Dirichlet L-function zeros exert a force pushing zeros from all other automorphic L-functions off the s=1 axis.

We have adapted the quantum relational Hoare logic originally proposed in (Unruh, POPL 2019) to incorporate "expectations" into preconditions and postconditions, thereby enabling the quantification of pre-/postconditions that reflect the relationship between programs' inputs and outputs when comparing pairs of programs.

The rapid transmission of contagious diseases is frequently intensified by a single high-transmission event, a super-spreader occurrence. This effect should be given considerable consideration in traditional epidemiological modeling, which requires reliable estimates of critical parameters such as $R_0$. We illustrate in this report that the effective $R_0$ value in such events is highly asymmetric and skewed towards higher values, with infinite variance, which also implies unpredictability of critical epidemic parameters. Given this understanding, we also outline the implications for predicting the epidemic's course and the feasibility of its containment through non-pharmaceutical interventions. The theoretical concepts described here are supported by numerical simulations and real-world data from recent historical events. The theoretical framework presented can be applied to various transmission scenarios and provides the basis for more accurate models accounting for super-spreader events, which is shown through an exemplification.

Let's consider a complex topological vector space, denoted as X, along with the collection L(X) of continuous linear operators that act on X. This paper seeks to expand the concept of codiskcyclicity, initially developed for a solitary operator within L(X), to a broader context of operator sets defined as $\Gamma\subset L(X).$ Some key results regarding codiskcyclic collections of operators are proven, accompanied by a codiskcyclicity criterion. Furthermore, we demonstrate its practical utility by investigating the codiskcyclicity of C_0-semigroups comprised of operators.

The paper addresses the problem of bias in vector magnetic field maps, particularly in estimating the component perpendicular to the line-of-sight, Bperp. This issue has been identified previously, but its implications have not been fully explored. We aim to provide a comprehensive examination of the sources of Bperp bias, considering various inversion methods, input data, and solar conditions. Through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations, we assess magnitude and potential variation in biased Bperp estimates. Additionally, we evaluate methods to mitigate this bias or methodically incorporate it into uncertainty estimates. Our findings 1) confirm that biased Bperp measurements overestimate magnetic field strength by a factor of four to ten on average, with up to a 500-fold overestimation in individual cases, and 2) propose a method based on Inverse-Weierstrass transformation to correct for this bias with correct values within a factor of two in 90 percent of cases. However, in regions of weak magnetic fields, we anticipate residual bias to persist even after correction.

A comprehensive analysis has been conducted to measure the radii of 6097 young star clusters in 31 galaxies from the LEGUS survey. The custom analysis pipeline allowed for a large and contamination-resistant sample, giving us the largest dataset to date of its kind. The study discovered that a vast majority of galaxies exhibit similar radii distribution patterns, with a notable peak at approximately 3 pc. The mass-radius relationship of star clusters in this sample follows a distinct $R_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto M^{0.24}$ pattern. Notably, this relationship applies uniformly to clusters under 1 Gyr old, albeit with a less pronounced slope in cases younger than 10 Myr. Theoretical models suggest that more massive star clusters tend to be nontidally constrained, expanding over time. The study further reveals that a substantial majority of these star clusters in the survey exhibit signs of gravitational binding, especially when viewed at older ages or greater masses. The study's results on the cluster density and surface density show substantial variation, however it seems the dispersion tends to lessen as the age of the cluster increases, where the densest of these youthful star clusters have a typical density of around 100 $M_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$.

We present a novel, direct method for calculating the decay width of hadrons
decaying to two photons, often requiring an indirect estimation via off-shell
form factors. The new method offers an uncomplicated way to study volume effects.
In an example calculation, we apply this approach to $\eta_c\rightarrow 2\gamma$.
Using lattice ensembles with three $N_f=2$ configurations at different lattice
spacings, we derive the final decay width $\Gamma_{\eta_c\gamma\gamma}=6.57(15)_{\textrm{stat}}(8)_{\textrm{syst}}$ keV,
considering systematics in the charm quark mass. This technique can be extended
to additional processes involving leptons and photons in final states.

A sign problem encountered in Monte Carlo simulations beyond half-filling can be mitigated by transforming the integration path. However, this transformation introduces an additional computational cost associated with the Jacobian determinant in the Boltzmann weight, posing a significant barrier for large-scale simulations. Our proposed architecture, based on a novel application of complex-valued affine coupling layers in neural networks, efficiently circumvents this challenge by achieving linear scaling of the determinant cost. As a result, this method allows us to tackle intractably large systems plagued by a severe sign problem.

This study provides fresh, precise estimates for the integral of the Dickman function $\pi(x,t) = \int_2^x \rho(x/t,u)du$, addressing questions from various researchers. Specifically, when $y = 2^{\log^* x - \log^* 6}$, we achieve an $\mathcal{O}(x)$ estimate with no dependence on $t$ in the Dickman function integral, matching the conclusion of a conjecture by various researchers. Additionally, we obtain a new, highly original bound in the extreme fractional power tower range for the Dickman function integral.

Given any non-erasing free monoid morphism σ and subshift X, its image subshift Y under σ and the associated complexity functions p_X and p_Y exhibit the following relationship: there exist constants c, d, and C, where p_X scales by a factor of at least c times d, while scaling at most C, in the sufficiently large integers n in N. If σ is recognizable and letter-to-letter, then p_Y and p_X grow at similar rates. However, if σ is not recognizable, then there exists an increase in complexity by at least a factor of 1.5. Furthermore, we can define the complexity function p_X and identify specific examples where complexity can increase dramatically, including a quadratic example to the extent of a quartet, demonstrating that a significant increase in complexity does not necessitate an increase to a higher order.

By leveraging previously acquired skills and adapting them to unfamiliar tasks without explicit guidance, humans demonstrate impressive cross-task capabilities.
This study aims to enhance the cross-task generalization ability of massive language models in unsupervised settings, with a focus on models like T0 and FLAN.
We introduce a novel, unsupervised retrieval-augmentation method known as ReCross, which leverages similar samples to boost performance on challenging tasks.
Unlike conventional retrieval-enhanced generation approaches that rely on labeled data, our method is entirely unsupervised and incorporates similar sample retrieval to improve model inputs and outputs.
We evaluate our method on 14 diverse tasks from 5 categories, utilizing the HumanEval dataset for unsupervised similar sample retrieval.
The experimental results show that ReCross consistently outperforms both baseline models and existing retrieval-augmented methods, with significant improvements of 8.4% and 10.6% on benchmark tests.

This research introduces the m-arcsinh Kernel ('m-ar-K') Fast Independent Component Analysis ('FastICA') approach ('m-ar-K-FastICA') for feature extraction, combining kernel-based dimensionality reduction with ICA to overcome the limitations of previous methods. Although the kernel trick offers a powerful way to tackle non-linearity, its effectiveness can be undermined by a lack of open-source and reproducible kernel implementations, especially those suitable for use with random data sets. The proposed m-ar-K-FastICA approach utilizes a readily available and adaptable C++ library, offering significantly enhanced performance and flexibility in feature extraction, especially when coupled with the SCIC evaluation metric for assessing extracted components. To further validate its efficacy, a comparison was made between the approach and other established methods, with results showcasing its superiority in producing highly non-Gaussian, non-linearly correlated data sets.

This work offers an overview of requirements engineering in the gaming sector.
Existing research studies on this topic have been comprehensively examined.
Key characteristics of the gaming industry were identified and their connections to broader market dynamics discussed.
In addition, several potential areas for further research within this field were briefly highlighted.

Optimizing hyperparameters in the private version of the stochastic gradient descent algorithm is a critical issue due to limited access to private datasets for hyperparameter tuning. The development of algorithms that efficiently find optimal hyperparameters for a favorable balance between privacy and performance within a predetermined search space is, therefore, crucial. In this paper, a generalized framework is established to determine an optimal balance between privacy and performance, and three cost-effective algorithms are systematically examined within this framework: evolutionary optimization, Bayesian methods, and reinforcement learning. The results of our experiments, conducted using MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets for hyperparameter tuning in private deep learning, show significant improvements over the conventional grid search method. The paper addresses existing challenges and potential research directions in the field, and provides an open-source code for hyperparameter tuning in private deep learning.

For a Coxeter system denoted by (W,S), we develop the concept of a boolean complex consisting of involutions within W, mirroring Ragnarsson and Tenner's previous work. By applying discrete Morse theory, we identify the homotopy type of this boolean complex for a significant subset of Coxeter groups, including finite groups, revealing that its homotopy type is equivalent to that of a collection of spheres with dimension |S|-1. Moreover, we derive straightforward, recursive formulas to compute the number of spheres within this collection.

The Euclid satellite, set to launch in 2022, will significantly influence future cosmological research with its Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer instruments. The authors of this study analyzed how correlated readout noise affects in-flight measurements for the NISP detectors and proposed an analytical method for noise covariance matrices. Through experimental data analysis, a 1/f-like noise model was fitted to the NISP engineering detectors and their noise characteristics were determined, allowing for more accurate flux measurements via maximum likelihood estimation. It was found that using this approach, a four-fold decrease in measurement bias using NISP in the near-IR compared to one using ENG would compare, with potential implications for exoplanet detection. The authors of this study also discussed how readout noise affects time domain analysis with Euclid and discussed the implications for NISP of active pixel behavior following a charge accumulation effect.

We applied an advanced statistical approach to examine the composition of 34,410 stars in the Milky Way disk using a already established model. Our analysis refined existing findings and offered several key insights: our study indicates that supernovae types, specifically prompt (Type Ia) and delayed (Types II, Ia), played a role in enriching the disk with elements, whereas over-enrichment by a factor of 2-3 in UV elements observed in data is unexplained; controlled exchange of material between disk components may account for this phenomenon; our results suggest that magnetic fields may require consideration when interpreting abundance data, especially for elements like Si, S, and Fe; discrepancies between our model and observations of outer disk stars may stem from neglected physical processes in modeling, with implications for abundance patterns in low-metallicity disk stars; and we argue that studying specific elements like O, Mg, Ar, Ni in the outer disk is essential to validate the current two-component model or reveal the influence of additional factors such as the star formation history.

The COVID-19 pandemic spread globally in early 2020 and caused severe consequences in China, also exacerbating public health anxiety fueled by rampant online rumors. To address this pressing issue, we examined the dynamics of rumor propagation and proposed a method to measure the impact of such misinformation. We focused on the "Fengshen" rumor related to the magical Fengshen Yanyi Tablets being found in Yiwu Market, Ningbo and sold on Taobao in late February 2020. Using the effective time and geographical distance between the initial discovery in China and the first reported sale in Taobao, we estimated the speed of online rumor propagation to be approximately 140 km/h. To validate our approach, we compared the calculated values of rumor transmission speed with actual data values from the effective time. Additionally, we provided practical applications of our method in assessing rumor spread and identifying the dynamics of public anxiety during the propagation process, thereby highlighting the significance of our analysis in managing public perception and mitigating the effects of misinformation during the pandemic.

A novel approach to measuring the distance to galaxies has been discovered by examining extragalactic planetary nebulae, specifically due to their nearly universal brightness pattern. Determining the precise distances to galaxies through planetary nebulae analysis depends on collecting comprehensive data sets, and the observed frequency of these nebulae directly correlates with the galaxies' overall mass. Therefore, researchers must either utilize wide-field observations or focus on the central regions of massive galaxies. Despite the observed distance estimates for some galaxies, a significant uncertainty persists as there's considerate variation associated with planetary nebulae properties. This research investigates whether the observed diversity can be explained using a simplified frequency distribution and also explores the potential for achieving more accurate distance determinations by expanding frequency data. Notably, a significant uncertainty persists solely by increasing frequency data for a specific galaxy, and re-evaluating existing findings demonstrates the potential for precise distance estimates with a sufficient data point size, and also the associated limitations.

Every day, hospitals around the world gather vast amounts of physiological data from their patients, leading to an escalating interest in conducting statistical analyses to provide better medical diagnoses. These analyses involve complex computations on significant datasets, necessitating high-performance data processing systems that can handle both existing and newly generated physiological data simultaneously. In this paper, we present LifeStream, a preprocessing tool designed for physiological data that extends conventional streaming engines like Spark and Flink. LifeStream takes into account the unique characteristics of physiological data, such as its diverse sampling rates, inherent data backlogs, and real-time generation. It also offers a suite of computation functions, such as missing value interpolation, waveform generation, and device-specific aggregations. LifeStream was prototyped by building upon Apache Spark and demonstrated significant performance improvements, offering up to an order of magnitude faster processing times for certain operations compared to batch processing, with minimal code differences. We also evaluated LifeStream by showcasing how it can facilitate statistical analyses on large-scale physiological datasets.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in higher dimensional space, do not fit the classification of Bertrand curves except in two-dimensional Euclidean space. A new category, called the timelike (1,3)-Bertrand curve, is defined to fill this gap and its characteristics are identified for curves in a four-dimensional Euclidean space.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is widely regarded as a key decision with far-reaching implications, given the numerous loss functions developed to date, making it crucial to carefully select one. Despite its significance, research on the topic often omits explicit justification for loss function selection. We contend that, like other crucial decision, loss function selection should be approached methodically, prioritizing function suitability for a given problem, rather than relying on convenience or de facto standards. To address this challenge, we put forward a novel approach to loss function selection based on a margin-based framework. Framework-based method enables us to systematically evaluate loss function components and derive new variants. Our approach yielded systematic improvement across diverse datasets, demonstrating its potential to enhance classification accuracy. Furthermore, our framework led to efficient replacement of complex metric learning frameworks, yielding comparable results with much lower computational cost.
A stabilizable boundary feedback controller is designed for the Navier-Stokes equations using a linear control scheme with an oblique boundary orientation.

This research aims to advance the understanding of thermomechanical behavior in polymer crystallization. Strain-induced crystallization plays a significant role in polymer mechanical and thermal properties and must be accounted for during production and final product application design. To effectively capture its mechanical and thermal impacts, the proposed model utilizes a unique decomposition approach to the deformation gradient and applies the Coleman--Noll procedure and minimum dissipation potential principle to material modeling. The resulting model includes suitable Helmholtz free energy and dissipation potential assumptions, which enables simulation of crystalline region formation, degradation, and temperature changes during cyclic loading tests. Numerical implementation based on the finite element method provides the basis for numerical solutions, which include simulations of material sample microstructure and temperature evolution.

To analyze the impact of external magnetization on doped Bi$_2$Se$_3$ with spin-triplet nematic superconductivity, we computationally investigate magnetic susceptibility in nematic and chiral superconducting states using the Ginzburg-Landau formalism near its critical temperature. A key observation in this analysis is that the superconducting order parameter shows a non-trivial response to the transverse component of an applied magnetic field, which can result in a paramagnetic response. Moreover, the topology of the Fermi surface exerts a substantial influence on magnetic susceptibility, with a specific Lifshitz transition inducing a transition from the nematic to the chiral phase and leading to the divergence of magnetic susceptibility at this transition point. Notably, the interplay between electron-electron interaction and competing phases of superconductivity is investigated, with results showing that the driving force behind a transition from the nematic to the chiral phase can be the presence of electron-electron interaction in the immediate vicinity of the transition. A comparison with existing experimental data is also presented in this analysis.

A primary issue in Imitation Learning (IL) is that the expert teacher's assessment of the agent's actions is rarely without flaw, significantly impacting the quality of feedback and, consequently, the quality of the teacher's evaluation. One effective solution is to train a student teacher to provide more accurate feedback than the original expert. However, existing research faces challenges due to the reliance on supervised classification, due to the absence of clear teacher feedback signals. A novel approach is presented in this paper, presenting a new exploration framework in which the agent can actively choose to gather high-quality data from an external, supreme expert, even a small increase in data access results in a significant increase in policy performance. The proposed framework achieves a notable improvement in performance, with small models showing at least a five-fold increase and large models showing at least a twenty-five-fold increase in score, when they are allowed to gather one percent of data from an external, supreme expert, even a small increase in data access results in a significant increase in policy performance. It's evident from these results that the proposed framework yields substantial gains from using external expert data.

Continuous phase modulation detection using conventional differential detection techniques is highly resistant to various channel disturbances, such as phase and Doppler shift. Its basic structure makes its implementation uncomplicated, involving the product of a received baseband signal and a time-reversed version of one symbol duration. Nevertheless, it experiences reduced signal-to-noise ratio compared to coherent detection methods. In this research, the performance of conventional differential detection is enhanced through increased delay periods. By accounting for $K$ symbol delays, the trellis structure and relevant branch and cumulative metrics are derived, resulting in an optimized criterion for $K$. This criterion is based on the minimum Euclidean distance between differential signals, ultimately facilitating the selection of ideal delay periods for popular CPM formats through simulated error rates verification.

New findings from 1D core-collapse simulations shed new light on the ultimate demise of massive stars, contradicting widely employed numerical models. This study delves into the implications of these discoveries for the formation of colliding black-hole - neutron-star binaries, including a notable candidate such as GW190426_152155 reported in the second Gravitational Wave Catalogue. Furthermore, it examines the influence of birth velocities and neutron star sizes on the generation of such systems, along with any potential electromagnetic counterparts associated with them. Models derived from these detailed core-collapse simulations predict a significantly higher rate of merger detections for BH-NS systems, about five to ten times higher than "standard" prescriptions, mainly due to the creation of low-mass BH through direct collapse, resulting in negligible natal kicks. The likelihood of observable systems producing an electromagnetic counterpart with these detailed supernovae engines ranges from two to twenty-five percent, contingent on uncertainties in the neutron star equation of state. Interestingly, in most BH-NS mergers with electromagnetic counterparts, the neutron star forms first, provided its radius remains under 12 kilometers. Core-collapse models anticipating low-mass BH formation with insignificant birth velocities increase the detection rate of similar candidates to approximately 10 percent, with most originating from coalescing black-hole and neutron-star pairs where the neutron star forms with little kick, or as isolated BH with subsequent neutron star capture.

A previously reported finding from the research of the 1990s suggests a connection between the variability of the vacuum state's energy and the speed of light. This connection is typically explained through the uncertainty principle and relies on dimensionality and the characteristics of massless particles' dispersion. Utilizing quantum field theory, this study determines an alternative expression for variance that doesn't depend on the properties of massless particles. This new formulation allows the concept of vacuum fluctuations to be applied to a wider range of theories. Furthermore, it demonstrates that the variability of the vacuum state's energy can be related to the fluctuation of a quantum field's particle number.

Current deep learning techniques for removing rain from images have achieved notable success in processing artificially created rainy images.  Nonetheless, their effectiveness drastically drops when confronted with genuine rainy conditions, primarily because they learn to eliminate rain based on assumptions rather than actual data.  Although some research has been conducted on subject-specific tasks, most approaches are confined to either image restoration or subject-transferable methods.  To address this limitation, we propose a new approach called DRRNet, a novel all-in-one solution that simultaneously restores rain-affected images and transfers clean rain patterns from a reference image.  Distinct from conventional all-in-one techniques that focus on symmetric information fusion, DRRNet uniquely employs a bifurcated network architecture to separately handle the complex tasks of restoration and transfer, avoiding the need for explicit rain pattern learning.  Moreover, we introduce a new evaluation framework for all-in-one images and evaluate numerous existing rain-restoring algorithms.  The results of our evaluation confirm the superiority of DRRNet over competing approaches, with impressive outcomes on both synthetic and real rainy images.

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their broader adoption is hindered by the expense and labor intensity of these comparisons. To overcome this limitation, we propose grouping multiple comparisons together and allowing human labelers to mark sub-regions of a condensed state space representation, thereby efficiently leveraging human time. Through data visualization techniques, we create an interactive interface for users to label these regions, thereby effectively enhancing the learning agents' performance, even when human labeling time remains constant, across basic Mujoco tasks.

We discuss recent research findings regarding model companions in set theory within the context of ongoing debates in the philosophy of mathematics. Initially, we explore how the concept of model companions is affected by the signature, before specifically examining the dependence of model companions in set theory. Our analysis indicates that the most intrinsic model companions for set theory correspond to $H_{\kappa^+}$ theories, as the infinite cardinal $\kappa$ varies. Furthermore, we highlight that the Continuum problem has a singular solution of $2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_2$, which aligns with some model companion of enriched set theory containing large cardinal axioms. This model-theoretic framework is justified by a maximality concept reminiscent of Hilbert's axiom of completeness.

This study establishes conditions and proof for a modified Kirchhoff-type equation,
designated as $(P_\lambda)$, which is influenced by a parameter $\lambda > 0$.
For any bounded domain $\Omega$, we demonstrate that $P_\lambda$ has solutions
for sufficiently large values of $\lambda$. Additionally, we identify specific
conditions under which $P_\lambda$ produces bounded solutions for these values of $\lambda$.

Evaluating a person's risk of drug abuse is crucial, and online surveys have proven effective for gathering relevant data. The data collection process included a comprehensive range of characteristics, including personality traits, impulsivity levels, and sensation seeking tendencies. The data set analyzed substance consumption patterns for 18 different central nervous system-altering substances. The research revealed that certain substances are frequently consumed in clusters, characterized by strong correlations, known as "pleiades." Notable clusters were identified around the substances ecstasy, heroin, and benzodiazepines. By exploring various classification techniques and features, a data-driven approach identified the most effective methods to categorize individuals as users or non-users for each specific substance or cluster. Among the techniques examined, including tree models and probability estimations, a top-performing classifier was chosen for each drug. The accuracy of these classifications exceeded 70 percent for nearly all substances when using a rigorous evaluation method. The best performance was seen for the substances cannabis, crack, ecstasy, legal highs, LSD, and volatile substance abuse, achieving a high classification accuracy of above 75 percent.

Our proposed dataset, ATOMIC, is an exhaustive collection of everyday commonsense reasoning rules comprising nearly a million text-based descriptions.  This atlas of inferential knowledge, structured as conditional relationships (if X, then Y), stands out from other available datasets that are centered on categorization, by providing a framework that accounts for causality and effects, actions versus thoughts, and intentional versus unintentional actions.  We have developed nine categories of these relationships and demonstrated the efficacy of incorporating these patterns into models of artificial intelligence.  Our findings reveal that through generative training on ATOMIC, our models have gained a capacity for basic reasoning about events that are novel.  This is supported by test results showing that machine learning models incorporating these patterns achieve more accurate outcomes in relation to models operating in isolation as judged by both automated assessments and human feedback.

Portfolio optimization is a critical application in Finance, yet its computational intricacies compel financial institutions to resort to approximations. We investigate the possibility of accelerating portfolio optimization using the HHL quantum algorithm. Building upon prior research, we aim to create a more efficient and practical approach to portfolio optimization that leverages the HHL algorithm. Specifically, we concentrate on applying the hybrid variant of the HHL algorithm to portfolio optimization, particularly in relation to portfolio liquidity.

To enhance data efficiency of state-of-the-art end-to-end ASR models and enable them to handle a large amount of unpaired text data through multi-modal training, it's essential to address two challenges: synchronizing the sampling rates of speech and language features and ensuring that the learned representations from both encoders are consistent. This paper introduces a novel bidirectional attention mechanism that combines the learning of both the ASR and text encoders using a multi-modal learning method. This attention mechanism facilitates the exchange of sampling rates, effectively allowing the quality of transformed features to be measured in an alternative space. This leads to speech representations being enriched with more linguistic information, while the text representations are made more similar to speech, enabling ASR models to effectively leverage unpaired text data for pretraining. Experimental evaluations on the Librispeech corpus reveal a significant 6.15% reduction in word error rate when only paired data is used and up to 10.79% when additional unpaired text data is applied.

This analysis addresses the challenge of optimizing cross-sectional area through a specific point within a given two-dimensional geometric form. To generalize this concept, the problem can be redefined in terms of cross-sectional area normalization through a given set of points within the shape. A key issue that arises is the non-convolutional nature of the problem, which hinders its solution. A practical solution to this problem is offered by using a polynomial approximation to solve the normalization problem. A necessary condition for optimal solution is also defined, and an iterative optimization method is offered to find the optimal solution. This method is proven to converge given specific conditions are met. A useful application of this approach is determining the central cavity of a two-dimensional geometric form. However, the method can also be applied to determine a given set of central points within the form.

function within the context of the classic cyclic one-dimensional parking problem.

formed from integers between 1 and n, and let P_n/\binom n m denote the

we aim to understand how the first k indices of a sequence, chosen from R_n/m
according to the uniform measure \mu, behave. Notably, this research reveals an

Measurements of superconducting nanowires, particularly NbN nanowires, indicate the presence of a critical voltage threshold for dc conduction below which coherent quantum phase slips dominate, potentially blocking conduction. The critical voltage of these nanowires is observed to be tunable using an adjacent gate electrode and varies significantly in response to applied voltage, aligning with expected results of quantum interference but exhibiting unanticipated periodic variations. The magnitude of these periodic variations far exceeds predictions based on capacitance alone and presents a discrepancy in understanding this phenomenon, especially after observing sudden period shifts during measurements. The possibility of attributing the behavior to granular Josephson junctions within the nanowires is also considered, offering an alternative explanation for the findings.

The discovery of T-dwarf GJ 229B in 1995 offered initial insight into its composition, yet a detailed analysis with current spectroscopic methods has been lacking, especially concerning its atmospheric features, which display unusual properties and contradict earlier estimates of the dwarf's mass and orbit, requiring further examination due to their implications for intermediate population object formation processes. With a distance of tens of astronomical units from its host star, GJ 229B exists near the boundary of the habitable zone, potentially offering an opportunity to study its atmosphere in greater detail with upcoming facilities. By applying the open-source retrieval suite AdvTomre to visible to sub-millimeter spectral data, researchers obtained consistent estimates of the dwarf's mass and effective temperature, as well as indications of its atmospheric structure, radius, chemical composition, and possible external influences from the host star. Unlike many of its counterparts, GJ 229B displays a contrary trend in water vapor absorption with increasing pressures, implying a divergent atmospheric profile that may result from the dwarf's low mass and relatively large radius. Furthermore, the retrieval results suggest a possible deviation from the dwarf's orbital plane, supported by evidence of alignment between other nearby objects. Although the data support an eccentric orbit, the analysis suggests that future observations and theoretical studies could provide more in-depth knowledge about the radius, mass, and formation processes of this unique object.

Our study offers an explanation of the structural properties of a thermal medium like quark-gluon plasma, using the framework of electron scattering via virtual photons on this medium. In particular, we investigate deep-inelastic scattering processes and derive moment sum rules from structure functions. These sum rules can be expressed as the thermal expectation values of twist-two operators, and such calculations are feasible using lattice QCD for a small set of initial moments. We demonstrate how lattice simulations can determine the minimum virtuality for a photon needed for Bjorken scaling to apply to structure functions. Additionally, we explain the parton model representation of the structure functions within the Bjorken limit and assess its coherence. This coherence can be quantified through a lattice-computable measure. Finally, we connect our theoretical framework to real-world experiments designed to probe the quark-gluon plasma created in heavy-ion collisions using semi-leptonic decays of heavy flavor hadrons produced in these collisions.

Our proposed approach tackles the challenge of novel view video prediction, taking input from multiple viewpoints. Unlike existing research that relies on narrow angle variations, our network can generate videos from significantly wider angles, up to 45 degrees, without the need for prior knowledge. By processing only RGB frames, we've developed a two-component representation, combining local and global features that enables novel view prediction. Our model achieves remarkable results on real-world datasets NTU-RGB+D and CMU Panoptic, surpassing the state-of-the-art in novel view video prediction, demonstrating significant gains in SSIM, PSNR, and FVD scores of 26.1%, 13.6%, and 60% respectively, without the use of prior views.

In this research, inter-orbital coupling was demonstrated using femtosecond laser writing, which enables orthogonal modes in a photonic lattice to couple with each other at different spatial locations. We characterized an asymmetric double-well structure, mapped its propagation dynamics and successfully created a device capable of spatial mode conversion anywhere within a photonic chip. Utilizing higher-order photonic mode phase structure, our experiment showed that a trimer configuration can serve as a $\pi$-phase beam splitter for multiplexing and other interference-based photonic applications.

The Ω-baryon, which contains sss quarks and has only been marginally detected in past experiments, has primarily been studied using theoretical methods so far. A study aims to explore this particle's properties utilizing a quark model with linear confining forces. Calculated resonance masses are presented for the ground and excited states of S, P, D, and F quark systems. A linear nature of the Regge trajectory, supported by calculated data and magnetic moments, has also been examined. This study compares its results to other approaches and available experimental evidence.

Airborne transmission risk in confined environments like buses is intricately affected by the interplay between turbulent airflow, respiration processes, coughing, and sneezing, as well as various ventilation methods, temperature-driven buoyancy effects, and surface deposition of aerosols. To better understand and quantify this complex dynamic, we used numerical models of unsteady airflow to analyze and visualize virus-laden aerosol transport. In comparing our detailed model to a widely accepted 'well mixed' model, notable discrepancies in the distribution of aerosol particles became evident, with implications for our understanding of the spread of airborne pathogens. Furthermore, the differences identified in our study are expected to be relevant to a broader range of enclosed settings beyond urban buses.

Building on cutting-edge experimental projects such as HIBEF at the XFEL, our calculations investigate the birefringent scattering of x-rays when interacting with two combined optical fields, a process known as the x-ray analog of the AC effect. To enhance this process, we propose utilizing linearly polarized laser fields polarized at a 45-degree angle to one another, which would result in an elliptically polarized combined field. To analyze this, we apply the Berghs and Berghs transformation, an established theoretical model. Consequently, this leads to the modification of x-ray photons as they gain effective mass in the laser field, resulting in the reversal of their spin state. Notably, the magnitude of this spin flip is influenced by the orientation of the magnetic field in relation to the laser fields, which can be seen by calculating the differential cross-section for x-ray photons in the lab frame. This in-depth study is made possible by the recent achievement of accelerating 100-kiloelectronvolt ion beams at the ETF experiment, which in turn enables a detailed comparative analysis of theoretical predictions and experimental observations, offering valuable insights for upcoming experiments at the ATF2.

This note outlines the algorithm devised by J. M. Eisenlohr and S. L. Farris to
systematically generate all fully transitive polyhedra in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Furthermore, this algorithm is employed to construct a novel polyhedron within three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Broadbent and Lord introduced the concept of unclonable encryption, a unique feature in an encryption scheme where an adversary can't produce two encrypted versions of the same original message from a given ciphertext. Our research expands upon this concept, focusing on several aspects:

  - Flexibility in Usage: We've identified a significant drawback in the previous unclonable encryption constructions by Broadbent and Lord, as they either only guarantee single-use security for ciphertexts or provide security for all adversaries but allow a limited amount of flexibility in decoding after re-cloning. Our contribution is an efficient construction of an essentially and softly clonable encryption scheme that provides both greater flexibility in usage.

  - Public Key Unclonable Encryption: We've made a breakthrough in the field by being the first to achieve publicly key secure unclonable encryption, with implications for the development of flexible, publicly key secure digital signatures.

  - Functional Cloning: We've identified a limitation in previous research, as it was unclear whether an adversary could create a copy of a given encrypted message that would return correct answers to any queried function, once again answering a question first posed by Broadbent and Lord in their work. Our contribution is an efficient construction of an unclonable encryption scheme that resists functional cloning, even if given access to an oracle that returns the original decoding of any queried function, for inputs in the set of all possible messages.

This study confirms that physical layer-based authentication is achievable in
Gaussian noise environments, with the caveat that an all-knowing adversary cannot be
beated. An examination of a model comprising encoder, decoder, and adversary was
carried out, with the latter possessing unlimited transmission capabilities and
unlimited access to the transmitted message. It was demonstrated that modifying an
existing communication protocol can enable secure transmission with negligible
effort. Notably, our findings reveal that secure communication can be accomplished
without providing the adversary any additional information, as long as they do not
already know something they shouldn't. Furthermore, our model allows for public
discussion between sender and receiver. A key finding of our research is that, in
certain instances, secure communication becomes impossible if the adversary has any
access to the message, but our model shows that this limitation can be overcome,
even with an all-knowing adversary, as long as they do not have access to the
transmitted message. Moreover, our results indicate that, in certain cases,
secure communication with an all-knowing adversary is possible if the encoder and
decoder possess prior knowledge, but not unlimited access to the transmitted message.

We utilized the full tight-binding model and random phase approximation to
explore flat-band plasmons in hole-doped twisted bilayer molybdenum disulfide.
Our calculations showed that lattice relaxation influences plasmon behavior.
When we considered intraband transitions, low-damped, flat plasmons emerged,
while accounting for interband transitions led to plasmon dispersion following
$\sqrt q$ law. The plasmon energies in these materials can be adjusted through
tweaking the twist angles and doping levels. For samples without lattice
relaxations, coexistence of low and high-energy plasmons occurs. Higher doping
levels however eliminate the quasi-flat plasmon. These observations imply that
two conditions must be satisfied: a flat band isolated from the other bands
and adequate doping level to witness the quasi-flat plasmon. The study offers
clues for exploring superconductivity mediated by plasmons in these materials.

This paper expresses the potential function $f$ associated with an almost conformal gradient Ricci soliton on a Sasakian manifold in terms of the scalar field $p$, determining when the potential function is constant, and establishing a link between $f$ and $\lambda$. We also establish a condition for a conformal Ricci soliton to be a gradient Ricci soliton, and provide a characterization of the soliton in terms of its contraction or expansion rate.

Both celestial bodies can experience mass loss due to an expansive outward flow,
often regulated or redirected by magnetic fields, as seen in the case of T Tauri stars.
The emergence of collimated high-speed streams, driven by interactions between
rotational and magnetic components, has already been observed in massive stars, but their
formation mechanism remains a critical area of study. Our computational simulations
utilizing linear magnetohydrodynamics successfully replicate streams by incorporating
ingredients such as angular momentum distribution, vertical magnetic field interaction,
mass ejection, and photoionization. The addition of ionization to low-mass stellar
simulations allows us to explore the potential for ionized high-speed streams on the
surrounding environment. These streams accelerate the rotation of any nearby circumstellar
material, while also shaping and modifying the surrounding accretion disk, producing
asymmetric structures and influencing the overall dynamics of the system. Our proposed
model thus provides a framework linking various phenomena, including asymmetric features,
magjetos, and high-speed streams, to explore their interconnected relationships.

The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect involves a rise in Spin-Orbit Coupling near a strong spin-orbit material's interface with an adjacent layer. This phenomenon has been observed in various systems, such as graphene and ferromagnetic layers, and controlling Spin-Orbit Coupling may lead to the discovery of novel phases in superconductor and semimetallic systems. In the study presented here, magnetoelectrical transport, specifically magnetic field-dependent resistivity and Hall resistance, were investigated in ultrathin platinum layers adjacent to vortex state superconductor lithium hydride. In contrast to thicker Pt samples, the sub-nanometer Pt layer showed a pronounced, vortex state-dependent "dome" in resistivity under a magnetic field, accompanied by resistance increase, likely due to the enhanced Spin-Orbit Coupling caused by the SOCP. This effect was not seen in a strong semimetallic system, mercury.

This paper provides approximate solutions to the fractional time-independent Schrödinger equation in $N$-dimensional space for a generalised Mie-type potential, expressed as $V(r^{\alpha})=A/r^{2\alpha} + B/r^{\alpha} + C$, with the fractional parameter $\alpha$ affecting the space variable $r$. As $\alpha$ equals 1, the potential becomes the original Mie-type potential, commonly studied in physics. Using the Jumarie type fractional derivative approach, solutions are obtained and expressed in terms of the Mittag-Leffler function and a fractionally defined confluent hypergeometric function. Verification of results is achieved by comparison with existing works, particularly for $\alpha=1$. Numerical examples, including a diatomic molecule, demonstrate energy eigenvalue and bound state eigenfunction calculations.

We analyze how enforcing a neural network's Lipschitz continuity, as it pertains to input sensitivity, affects its performance. In order to investigate this, we developed a straightforward approach to determine the upper bound for a neural network's Lipschitz constant, taking into consideration various $p$-norms commonly used. This approach enables us to frame training a neural network with a limited Lipschitz constant as an optimisation problem that can be resolved via constrained stochastic gradient descent. We validate our method by assessing it on multiple datasets and noting that using a different input norm than the output norm can substantially lower training losses and enhancement is particularly apparent when using the Manhattan norm.

Sequential neural network models are highly versatile in addressing NLP tasks.
Their sequential design leads to fundamental questions regarding their capacity
to learn complex language hierarchies and grammatical patterns naturally
occurring in human language.
As a case study for understanding the implicit comprehension of sentence
structure and the adoption of a complex yet systematic morphological system,
we explore agreement prediction in Basque, which demands a thorough analysis
of sentence structure and the ability to manage multiple forms of verb
agreement suffixes.
Our analysis of sequential models' performance on a comprehension-based
dataset and our morphological analysis of the results indicate that current
neural network models are capable of capturing basic principles of sentence
structure and solving agreement prediction.
However, their proficiency varies significantly between Adj-N and Plu-Acc
predictions due to differences in data frequency.
Our exploratory analysis also indicates that current neural network models
perform differently on Adjective-Noun and Plural-Accusative predictions when
compared to similar word order issues in English, unlike the outcomes observed
withadapting models to mimic human performance.

HD80606b, a planet that passes directly in front of its host star, undergoes a significant 1000-fold increase in the heat it receives due to its highly eccentric 111-day orbit. As the planet rapidly moves close to its star, its surface temperature jumps dramatically from 400K to over 1400K in a matter of hours during its closest approach. Observations using the James Webb Space Telescope will soon take advantage of this planet's extraordinary environment to study various aspects of its atmosphere. Accurate information about HD80606b's orbit is essential to make the most out of these observations. Researchers have conducted in-depth analyses of the planet's transits on February 7, 2020, and December 13, 2021, along with the timings of its closest approach to its star over the past two decades. These observations and new orbital data will be utilized in preparing observations for the JWST, but in order to do so, researchers need precise information about the planet's long-term change in its average distance from its star, periastron angle, and the shape of its orbit. As highly moving planets can have complicated orbital paths due to various factors, including the influence of other celestial bodies, gravitational interactions, and the transfer of angular momentum, it's necessary to carefully consider these elements in order to accurately understand the planet's orbital behavior. Customized digital games successfully encourage motivation in repetitive exercises required for motor rehabilitation; nevertheless, developing adjustments that cater to both therapy and enjoyment objectives poses a challenge. To tackle this issue, we propose an approach where an initial statistical model of game performance identifies specific settings that mirror players' typical behavior, even in the face of diminished control. This approach is exemplified through a practical application involving upper limb rehabilitation and a specially designed controller for the Pac-Man game. Collaborative sessions between occupational therapists and game developers resulted in the identification of two key factors that affect the gameplay experience and influence rehabilitation adjustments. Experimental measurements of the participants' interaction with the modified game revealed that our low-latency statistical model accurately identifies optimal parameter values that reproduce baseline gameplay under controlled conditions. This methodology holds potential for addressing balance problems related to the customization of engaging games, particularly when guided by user feedback within a well-defined parameter space.

Our research offers a variational approximation, drawing from the Ambrosio-Tortorelli model, to quantify brittle fracture energies in complex, piecewise-rigid structures, applicable to both nonlinear and linearised elasticity frameworks.

We investigate the possibility of lepton-flavour non-universality in certain processes at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). To this end, we focus on Drell-Yan ditau production and calculate precise corrections to this process, taking into account the effects of quantum chromodynamics at the next-to-leading order. A specialized code is developed to efficiently generate these corrections, allowing for more accurate simulations of ditau events. By applying these simulations to recent LHC data, we can place constraints on a type of exotic particle, known as vector leptoquarks, based on their mass and coupling strength. This code is an important tool for ongoing and future searches for vector leptoquarks at the LHC, particularly those involving the collision of protons at high energies.

Radiation exposure during positron emission tomography (PET) scans restricts their usage for sensitive groups, such as pregnant women and young individuals requiring frequent imaging, due to compromised image quality from lower doses or shortened scan times. Deep-learning models have made significant advancements in enhancing PET images by translating low-quality PET scans with associated MRI data to higher-quality PET images, particularly with significantly reduced doses. Nonetheless, such deep learning approaches have primarily focused on utilizing training datasets similar to their test data, neglecting evaluation of their performance for new acquisitions outside of their development domains. Therefore, our study assesses whether existing high-performance PET images translation methods can generalize to unseen data scenarios, including various scanners and dose settings. To conduct this evaluation, we utilized datasets spanning multiple scanners and data distributions for model testing, such as high-dose PET-MRI and Prussian Blue PET data, despite using them exclusively once during the training process. Our experimental results showed a lack of generalizability in such PET image-enhancing deep learning approaches when applied to such unseen data domains.

While data collection and automation have fueled the success of personalization systems, they have sparked serious concerns regarding privacy. People's worries about their data and how it's utilized often hinder the adoption of these systems, mainly due to a lack of transparency. Existing research into privacy-metric development and user attitudes is concentrated in the marketing sector, leaving the tourism industry underserved. This study explores tourists' perceptions and attitudes towards data collection and personalization within tourism platforms. Our research findings, gathered through an online survey, reveal that tourists are willing to share their information for a better experience but are eager for full transparency in how their data is used to create a personalized plan. Furthermore, we investigate potential metrics for measuring and enhancing user-perceived privacy in personalization systems, as well as strategies for balancing user privacy with the accuracy of recommendations.

A type of analytical framework, known as centering theory, is used to examine the structural organization of written texts, particularly human-authored documents. This theory focuses on analyzing discourse through the examination of individual sentences and their relationships. A key aspect of these frameworks involves identifying the most prominent element within each sentence to determine its functional role. This research investigates automatic text coherence prediction models by evaluating their performance across languages with differing grammatical structures, resulting from varying theoretical approaches to modeling, namely the structural and functional perspectives. Our experiments reveal that models performing best are not consistently tied to a specific perspective, with optimal results achieved through a combination of both perspectives for low-resource languages. This research also demonstrates that current coherence prediction models tend to excel at texts written in English but struggle with human-written texts outside of English.

We have devised three new parameterized algorithms for identifying whether a directed graph can be represented in an upward planar layout. Specifically, we've developed a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the number of source vertices, an XP algorithm based on the graph's treewidth, and a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the treedepth parameter. Our novel method combines parameterized techniques with SPQR tree-decompositions, extending previous tractability findings on series-parallel graphs, single-source graphs, and outerplanar graphs.
